title: SLI fabric patterns for short-lived inference flows
summary: Working draft: compact patterns for constructing SLIs, trace anchors, and dashboard slices tailored to short-lived token inference requests (low-latency, high-throughput paths). Focus: quantify end-to-end perceived latency, cache-warmth effects, and fallback regressions.
background: Operations + serving-runtime have recurrent incidents where surface latency rises but token-level metrics look fine. Hypothesis: multi-hop internal calls, KV cache miss amplification, and fallback fanout cause user-visible pain. Need a reproducible SLI fabric that links traces, probe slices, and dashboards for quick RCA.
goals:
1) Define 3 minimal SLIs that reflect user-perceived latency for short-lived inference calls.
2) Standardize trace annotation patterns (span tags and trace anchors) so dashboards can stitch session context.
3) Provide dashboard panel recipes and alert thresholds that prioritize high-confidence signals and limit noise.
4) Produce quick onboarding notes for oncall to use these panels during rollouts.
slis: perceived_ttfu_95: time from request-received to first-byte-to-client (p95) aggregated by route and tenant
response_tail_p99_normalized: p99 of end-to-end response time excluding requests >5s (flag long tails separately)
cold_start_penalty_index: ratio of p95 with kv_cache_miss=true vs kv_cache_hit=true over rolling 1h
trace_guidelines:
Span tagging conventions:
- root.span.attributes['route'] = logical route name
- span['kv.cache_hit'] = true|false
- span['fallback_model'] = <variant> if model fallback occurred
- annotate span with 'probe_id' for synthetic probes to glue traces to dashboards
Trace anchors:
- mark entry span with 'client.session_id' and 'request_token_count'
- create a short-lived 'service-check' span when a fallback path is invoked
Sampling:
- sample all spans for errors and any request with kv_cache_miss=true
- adaptive sampling for high-throughput routes: deterministic sample 1% plus all anomalies flagged by anomaly-detector
dashboard_playbook:
Panel grouping:
- Group A: user-visible SLIs (perceived_ttfu_95, p99 response tail)
- Group B: cache-warmth metrics (kv_hit_rate, cold_start_penalty_index)
- Group C: internal fanout (avg_parallel_model_calls, fallback_rate)
Alert rules (suggested):
- page if perceived_ttfu_95 > 350ms for two consecutive 5m buckets AND fallback_rate > 2%
- notify if cold_start_penalty_index > 1.6 for 30m
Widget notes:
- add a sparkline of p95 p95/median ratio to spot skewing quickly
- include trace-links column in the operator table (link to trace tool with trace id)
Query cost control:
- use precomputed rollups for p95 and p99, fallback to raw for on-demand drilldowns
- limit trace link generation to sampled sessions to avoid cost explosion
open_questions: Scope: should 'perceived_ttfu_95' include time spent in client network (yes for public hosted API) or only internal runtime?
Threshold tuning: what is the baseline p95 per-route? need baseline sweep across last 90 days (who owns?)
Sampling budget: can we reserve 100qps of full-span traces for each critical route during business hours?
